what: Virtu Financial is a market maker. Its computers quote prices on shares, currencies, commodities and crypto all day, earning a small spread on each of millions of trades, and it also sells execution services to clients.
customers: Retail brokers whose orders it fills, and institutions using its trading and analytics services.
money: earning the spread on trades across asset classes
agency trading and workflow technology for institutions
moat: Technology and connections to hundreds of venues built over years, plus the scale to quote continuously: market making rewards the fastest and best-capitalised participants and punishes everyone else.
risks: Earnings rise with volatility and fall when markets are calm
Payment for order flow, which routes retail trades to firms like Virtu, is periodically under regulatory review
opportunities: 8.5 times earnings with $879M of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $2.3B to $3.6B in two years as volatility and retail trading rose
Crypto and options market making are growing faster than equities
watch: Adjusted net trading income per day, and any regulatory move on order flow payments.
